Each probe uses **only** the feature set described to test whether trivial patterns separate the classes.

| b) Border strips only | 0.7764 | 0.0116 | 0.7917, 0.7595, 0.7726, 0.7714, 0.7869 |
| c) Intensity stats only | 0.7421 | 0.0171 | 0.7714, 0.7440, 0.7250, 0.7452, 0.7250 |

### Interpretation

⚠️  **SHORTCUT RISK FLAGGED** for probe(s): `a) 32x32 thumbnail`.

| Probe | CV Acc | Risk |
|-------|--------|------|
| a) 32x32 thumbnail | 0.9257 ± 0.0046 | 🔴 >90% |
| b) Border strips only | 0.7764 ± 0.0116 | 🟢 ≤90% |
| c) Intensity stats only | 0.7421 ± 0.0171 | 🟢 ≤90% |

**Interpretation:**
- A probe accuracy >90 % on **thumbnail** (a) means coarse pixel patterns alone separate classes, suggesting strong acquisition-level differences (e.g. different scanners, exposure settings) rather than purely pathological signal.
- A probe accuracy >90 % on **border strips** (b) strongly suggests image-level artefacts such as metadata text overlays, padding colour or scanner borders that correlate with label — a source-domain shortcut.
- A probe accuracy >90 % on **global intensity stats** (c) indicates systematic brightness/contrast differences between classes at the dataset level, pointing to acquisition protocol differences.  Models trained without normalisation may exploit this rather than learning anatomy.

**Recommended mitigations:** histogram equalisation or CLAHE, aggressive border cropping, mixed-source data collection, and dataset-unbiased evaluation.
